questions.q: Who was Duke of Milan before Antonio took over?
Who is Prospero's daughter?
Which spirit serves Prospero?
Whose island was it before Prospero arrived?
Who is Antonio's ally, the King of Naples?
Whom does Miranda fall in love with?
What does Prospero create at the start of the play?
What does Ariel want most?
What does Prospero give up at the end?
questions.a: His magic (he breaks his staff and drowns his book)

questions.q: Which value does Prospero choose over vengeance?
questions.a: Virtue, forgiveness ('The rarer action is / In virtue than in vengeance')

questions.q: How does Shakespeare present forgiveness in The Tempest?
questions.a: Indicative: 'The rarer action is / In virtue than in vengeance'; Prospero's power then mercy; Ariel's pity changes him; Antonio's silence (forgiveness may not change everyone); breaking the cycle of betrayal.

passage.title: Into the Storm
paras: When the call comes, the volunteers drop everything. A lifeboat crew member may be eating dinner, sitting in a classroom or fast asleep, yet within minutes the boat is in the water, heading towards danger that everyone else is sailing away from.

Around the coasts of the UK and Ireland, most lifeboat crews are unpaid. They train for hundreds of hours to handle the boat in waves taller than a house, to give first aid in the dark and to pull a frightened swimmer from freezing water.
Why do they do it? Ask them, and most give the same short answer: because someone needs help. One volunteer put it simply: 'You never know whose child is out there.'
Their work is a reminder that courage is not the absence of fear. It is choosing to help even when you are afraid.

questions.q: Give two facts about lifeboat crews.
questions.a: Any two: most are unpaid; they train for hundreds of hours; they launch within minutes.

questions.q: What is the writer's view of the volunteers? Give evidence.
questions.a: Admiring: 'courage is not the absence of fear'; they head towards danger.

questions.q: Explain one method the writer uses and its effect.
questions.a: Contrast (sailing towards danger others sail away from); the quotation from a volunteer; the list of everyday situations; effect explained.

questions.q: How does the idea of courage in the article link to The Tempest?
questions.a: E.g. choosing to forgive is a brave choice for Prospero, like choosing to help despite fear.
